newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New UN rights envoys to Somalia, Colombia, Abkhazia.
newsitem.headline: New UN rights envoys to Somalia, Colombia, Abkhazia.

text.p: The United Nations on Friday announced the appointment of a human rights expert on Somalia, and heads of new monitoring offices in Colombia and Abkhazia.

U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Jose Ayala Lasso appointed Mona Rishmawi, a Palestinian lawyer at the International Commission of Jurists, as his independent expert on Somalia, according to a statement.

Rishmawi will try to implement U.N. advisory human rights services for Somalia aimed at "re-establishing respect for human rights and the rule of law, and strengthening the police and the judicial and prison systems in a manner consistent with internationally accepted criminal justice standards", it said.
She plans a mission to London and Nairobi between February 2-7, and "if conditions permit, she also wishes to travel to Mogadishu," the statement said.
Rishmawi succeeds Samuel Jajiretundu-Kozonguizi of Namibia.

Ayala-Lasso, whose U.N. Human Rights Centre in Geneva oversees 13 field offices employing 250 people, also named Spanish diplomat Almudena Mazarrasa Alvear as director of the U.N. human rights office in Colombia, which opened in November.
He named Swedish diplomat Elisabeth Stam as director of the U.N. human rights office opened last month in Abkhazia, Georgia.
